title: SaaS and subscription businesses
baseline_summary: Existing coverage includes provider/customer role boundaries, subscription timing, hosted implementation, principal-agent, future ASU 2025-06 timing, and synthetic provider/customer close examples. The baseline is not evidence of complete SaaS treatment.

questions.question: How does advance billing/cash differ from earned deferred subscription revenue, and how do customer credits/refunds change the close?
questions.finding: Current EY interpretation distinguishes advance contract liabilities, expected refunds, service-level concessions and material rights/options; usage of a future-service credit is not automatically revenue or a refund. Classification still depends on enforceable contract terms, usage/credit records and any remittance duty.
questions.remaining_gap: No actual credits, customer contract population, expected-refund estimate or unclaimed-property analysis was available. Current consolidated ASC text was not directly verified; the observed browser limitation is not evidence of paid-access necessity.

questions.question: How are SaaS contract modifications and blend-and-extend renewals accounted for?
questions.finding: Current EY interpretation updates the general framework: separate-contract treatment requires added distinct service priced at standalone selling price; otherwise assess remaining-service distinctness and apply prospective or catch-up accounting as indicated. A blended price alone does not decide the outcome.
questions.remaining_gap: No renewal or modification contract was tested, and the public firm guidance is not authoritative FASB text.

questions.question: When should usage-based fees be recognized, and how do credits/minimums/rollovers affect it?
questions.finding: Usage-fee guidance distinguishes period-specific allocation when usage pricing faithfully depicts service delivered from estimating variable consideration and recognizing it over the service period subject to constraint. Minimum commitments, tiers, unused credits and rollover rights require their contract terms and may implicate a material right or breakage.
questions.remaining_gap: No minimum/rollover agreement or live usage population was inspected; public interpretation does not choose entity-specific terms or resolve current consolidated Topic 606.

questions.question: Which sales commissions qualify for capitalization and how should renewal commissions be amortized?
questions.finding: No new evidence in this follow-up. The prior source-supported general rule remains: qualifying incremental costs of obtaining a contract are capitalized when recoverable, subject to the practical expedient; amortization follows related transfer of services.
questions.remaining_gap: Commission plan, renewal commensurateness, clawback terms, expected customer life and impairment remain entity-specific.

questions.question: How do provider development, customer's hosted implementation and internal-use software capitalization differ?
questions.finding: ASU 2025-06 retains management authorization/funding plus probable completion and intended use, and requires an assessment of significant development uncertainty. The probable threshold is not met until such uncertainty is resolved; examples include novel/unproven functionality not resolved by coding and testing, or significant performance requirements not identified or continuing to be substantially revised. The amendment is future-effective for most calendar-year entities absent early adoption.
questions.remaining_gap: Provider ASC 985-20 versus 350-40 classification, actual entity election/adoption and project evidence still require review; the ASU is issued update text, not the entire current Codification.

recommended_additions: Add separate workpaper populations for deferred subscription service, prepaid usage rights, concessions/refunds and breakage, with contract-specific flags for term, rollover, minimum, refundability, material right and unclaimed-property obligation.
Enrich provider software-cost coverage with ASC 985-20 technical-feasibility evidence and a hosted-only SaaS classification decision branch, labeling KPMG as interpretive rather than authoritative.
Add a workpaper connecting subscription contract/version, service period, usage events, billings/cash, contract liability, modification and commission assets.
unresolved_gaps: Current consolidated ASC 606/340-40 text, service-contract and IP license tests, and entity-specific policy/adoption.
No entity contract tested for usage credits, service-level credits, refunds, rollovers, minimums, renewal rights, or state unclaimed-property requirements.
Provider hosted-only software-cost classification under ASC 350-40 versus ASC 985-20 remains fact-specific despite new KPMG interpretive coverage.
Tax, state SaaS/digital sales tax, enforceability, and non-US VAT.
priority_rationale: SaaS revenue depends on contract/version/usage evidence and subscription providers often have material deferred balances and commission assets; filling the specific evidence gaps improves decision support without duplicating existing overview coverage.

title: E-commerce and marketplace sellers
baseline_summary: The existing trade guide and synthetic reconciliation already cover ownership, POS, returns, inventory, card clearing, settlement, and mutually exclusive marketplace principal/agent branches. The fixture excludes state sales tax and real platform evidence.

questions.question: How does a marketplace/processor settlement reconcile to sales, returns, tax, fees, reserves, receivables and bank cash?
questions.finding: Current Stripe report/API documentation supports a row-level reconciliation from balance activity through payout and bank, with source IDs, gross/fee/net, status, created/available dates and payout association. A labeled synthetic example ties to $8,985 available-funds payout under its stated assumptions; the $250 hold and $50 release transfer available/reserve balances and leave $200 held. IRS 1099-K gross information reporting is not the provider net settlement or GAAP revenue.
questions.remaining_gap: No actual account, statement, bank match, merchant terms, tax return or transaction population was available. Synthetic numbers are illustrative, not seller evidence; reserve presentation and tax/revenue treatment remain terms- and fact-dependent.

questions.question: How should post-sale returns, refunds, credits, chargebacks and dispute fees be distinguished?
questions.finding: Shopify documents that a refund may occur without a physical return and restocking is optional; Stripe distinguishes an issuer/network chargeback and balance debit from a seller refund. EY current interpretive guidance addresses refund liabilities and the separate recovery asset when expected inventory returns. The settlement event alone does not determine sale reversal, loss, fee, return or inventory recognition.
questions.remaining_gap: No seller/processor agreement, card-network rulebook, dispute case, return inspection or customer evidence was inspected; current Codification and entity policy need application.

questions.question: How should third-party fulfillment/custody, physical inventory and platform/storage/fulfillment fees be separated?
questions.finding: Amazon’s FBA inventory API identifies fulfillable, inbound, reserved, unfulfillable and researching populations, useful for status reconciliation. These fields do not establish title, existence, condition, valuation or cut-off. A dated AE/English contract was read only as a foreign comparator and is excluded from U.S. findings.
questions.remaining_gap: No U.S. seller agreement, actual FBA inventory response, 3PL confirmation, inventory ledger or physical count was inspected; ownership/control and fee accrual remain entity-specific.

questions.question: Which party collects/remits sales tax on marketplace sales and what reporting obligations remain?
questions.finding: The existing California facilitator source remains the only state-specific tax authority reviewed. The IRS 1099-K page adds the distinct federal gross-payment reporting rule but does not establish who must collect/remit state sales tax. Keep facilitator status and residual seller filing/record obligations separate from revenue and net settlements.
questions.remaining_gap: No national or 50-state review, current nexus thresholds or product taxability analysis was performed; governing jurisdiction and channel facts remain necessary.

questions.question: When is the seller/marketplace gross principal versus net agent?
questions.finding: No new evidence in this follow-up. The prior FASB source supports assessing control of each specified good/service before transfer; gross principal/net agent presentation does not follow from payout routing, tax facilitator role or fulfillment service alone.
questions.remaining_gap: Actual contract, specified promise, inventory/control facts and transfer terms were not available for an entity conclusion.

recommended_additions: Add source-backed settlement adapters for Shopify Payments, Amazon Flat File V2 and Stripe that map fields only to evidence populations, not presumed accounting entries.
Add a 3PL/FBA inventory tie-out with SKU/FNSKU mapping, inbound receipts, fulfillable/reserved/unfulfillable/researching, shipment/return/damage and physical-count differences.
Keep transaction recognition, principal-agent, return liability/recovery asset, processor fee, dispute loss and sales tax as separate accounting decision layers.
unresolved_gaps: Actual merchant statements/API responses, Amazon Inventory Ledger, 3PL confirmations and merchant contracts.
Chargeback/network rules and evidence for the status and accounting of each dispute.
Current state-by-state facilitator/nexus/product tax rules; California is sole jurisdiction read.
The new vendor docs specify workflow but do not settle GAAP treatment, inventory ownership, valuation or title.
priority_rationale: Existing corpus already has a strong merchant role and settlement fixture. Incremental work should target missing platform evidence and tax jurisdiction coverage rather than another generic retail example.

title: Oil and gas operators and nonoperators
baseline_summary: Existing corpus substantively separates operator, nonoperator, mineral royalty owner, contractor, purchaser settlement, ONRR reporting, dated SEC cost method, synthetic depletion, and historical ARO boundaries. The same current 2025 IRS partner K-1 instructions are also represented by corpus source src_family_office_irs_k1_1065_2025 (shared research key cp_irs_k1). It does not contain detailed current JIB procedure or legal title evidence.

questions.question: How should operator JIB chargeability and nonoperator review/audit connect to actual agreements and evidence?
questions.finding: NOG’s 2025 filing distinguishes its nonoperator role from operator advances expected to be applied to JIBs; SM Energy discloses receivables from co-owners for JIB charges. These actual filings improve the operator/nonoperator workpaper map, but neither establishes chargeability, overhead, audit timing or contractual rights under another party’s JOA. COPAS MFI-40 remains a July 2023 committee-approved draft without verified adoption.
questions.remaining_gap: No signed JOA/accounting procedure, final MFI-40, JIB invoice, underlying support or audit exception schedule was available. Contract chargeability and adjustment deadlines remain entity-dependent.

questions.question: How do purchaser sales, operator cash, revenue distributions, royalty and transport differ?
questions.finding: SM Energy’s 2025 revenue disclosure links production revenue to purchaser delivery/control and separately describes co-owner JIB receivables. Existing ONRR instructions separately identify federal/Indian royalty reporting and allowances. Together these support the general boundary among commodity sale, operator cash, co-owner cost recovery, royalty remittance and revenue presentation.
questions.remaining_gap: Purchaser agreements, title/transport terms, WI and net-revenue decks, private/state royalty terms and an actual settlement were not inspected.

questions.question: How do ownership changes affect billed costs, proceeds and mineral interests?
questions.finding: NOG public transaction filings show completed acquisition dates can differ from stated effective dates and separately identify a nonoperator WI versus the operator’s share. The Texas FAQ notes a payor may require a division order with effective date, decimal/type and other fields, but says it does not amend the JOA or lease and that the RRC lacks lease/royalty authority. These facts support separately dated ownership and payment decks, not a legal cutover conclusion.
questions.remaining_gap: No executed assignment, title opinion, lease, JOA, purchaser deck, division order or property ledger was inspected. RRC material is informal, Texas-specific and not title authority.

questions.question: Which financial reporting cost method, depletion and abandonment rules apply?
questions.finding: NOG’s 2025 10-K demonstrates a disclosed full-cost policy; SM Energy’s 2025 10-K demonstrates successful efforts. SM’s UOP denominator differs by pool: drilling/completion and field development costs use estimated net proved developed reserves, while proved leasehold costs use total net proved reserves. Existing dated SEC rules and IRS materials remain separate SEC-regulatory and federal tax references.
questions.remaining_gap: The examples do not select a reporting entity’s method or establish current consolidated SEC/ASC detail; its policy, eligibility, engineering reserve estimates, pool costs, ceiling/impairment and taxpayer basis/limits remain unverified.

questions.question: How are ARO and remediation distinguished, and how do GAAP, tax and royalty/regulatory amounts differ?
questions.finding: Current EY and Deloitte public interpretation distinguishes retirement-related legal ARO obligations from environmental remediation associated with improper operation/catastrophic events. NOG and SM Energy disclose current company-specific ARO policies and estimates. FAS 143 in the corpus is historical only, not current ASC.
questions.remaining_gap: No obligation instrument, current authoritative ASC text, asset-level ARO calculation, permit, state bond, tax return or remedial claim was reviewed. Scope, legal obligor, timing, rate and later estimate changes depend on facts and applicable law.

questions.question: Can ONRR royalty rate/allowance and gross transport amount be substituted with WI or division-order percentages?
questions.finding: Existing ONRR Release 4.5 keeps federal/Indian volume, value, payor, rate and transportation/processing allowances separate. The Texas FAQ’s limited division-order/payor decimal information adds one state-specific distinction. Neither ONRR rates/allowances nor a payee decimal substitutes for WI or GAAP revenue.
questions.remaining_gap: Only federal/Indian ONRR and a Texas FAQ were examined; private leases, other states, actual report months, well interests and legal rights require their own sources and facts.

recommended_additions: Add a JIB/nonoperator audit schedule keyed to the signed procedure, property, cost class, approval, overhead basis, adjustment window, support and ownership-effective date; treat MFI-40 only as an unverified proposal.
Add a separate federal tax depletion reference clearly marked taxpayer-level, with cost versus percentage depletion and entity/partner reporting distinction, not a GAAP calculation.
Maintain separately linked GAAP, tax, SEC, private royalty, ONRR and state-regulatory populations.
unresolved_gaps: Final/current COPAS interpretation and paid procedure details; MFI-40 adoption status is unverified.
Current ASC 932 and 410/450 full Codification plus entity-specific method/adoption.
JOA/lease/title/division order, state pooling and legal ownership facts.
Reserve engineering, GAAP depletion/full-cost ceiling, tax basis and tax eligibility. IRS source adds general federal tax distinctions only.
State severance tax, private royalty, plugging and environmental requirements.
priority_rationale: The corpus has a mature synthetic production/royalty/ARO boundary example; concrete operator/nonoperator JIB and effective-dated ownership procedures are the highest-value additions while preserving contractual, financial reporting, tax, and royalty bases as distinct.
